themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 6.61)—suggesting a potential widespread ventilation or indoor pollution event affecting multiple residential units in CD 202.
evidence: 7 indoor air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 6.61, severity: high)
Coincides with uptick in rodent complaints (6 THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 avg) and unsanitary conditions, suggesting linked environmental degradation
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints cluster in specific buildings or blocks—could indicate HVAC failure, mold outbreak, or external pollution source
Interview residents experiencing air quality issues; consult NYC Dept of Health on whether mold, lead paint dust, or outdoor air pollution (industrial activity in South Bronx corridor) is driver
Cross-reference with DOB permit data to identify buildings with deferred maintenance or lack of ventilation upgrades

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 1.5 per week over 8 weeks—a 300% spike (z-score: 4.5)—indicating accelerating pest pressure in residential and commercial spaces across Hunts Point/Longwood.
evidence: 6 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.5, severity: high)
Aligns with spike in unsanitary conditions (514 total complaints over 90 days) and indoor air quality complaints, suggesting compound environmental neglect
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to determine if outbreak is building-specific (failed pest control contracts) or neighborhood-wide (gap in city enforcement or waste management)
DOB data shows 185 alteration permits filed in 90 days—investigate whether renovation activity is displacing rodents or whether buildings lack pest prevention infrastructure
Interview residents and tenant advocates; verify whether landlords are responding to complaints; check DOB inspection records for violations

themes_detail.label: Curb and Street Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—signaling rapid physical infrastructure decay in public rights-of-way that could affect pedestrian safety and traffic flow.
evidence: 3 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69, severity: high)
2300% spike from 8-week baseline, largest percentage increase in dataset
Complements spike in illegal parking complaints (599 total over 90 days), suggesting curb management challenges districtwide
reporting_angles: Verify: Are complaints concentrated on specific streets/corridors? Site visit to assess actual curb damage (pothole depth, edge fracturing, drainage impact)
Check Department of Environmental Protection/Sanitation schedules for street repair and sweeping in CD 202; assess adequacy of resource allocation
Interview community board members about deferred maintenance backlog; cross-reference with CB budget requests for street/infrastructure funding

themes_detail.label: Elevator Failures in Multi-Family Buildings
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints peaked at 22 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 7.6 per week—a 188% spike (z-score: 4.07)—affecting resident mobility and safety, particularly acute for elderly and disabled residents in aging multi-family stock.
evidence: 22 elevator complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 7.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.07, severity: high)
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request for 'assign additional building inspectors'—chronic maintenance gap in aging building stock
reporting_angles: Which buildings had multiple complaints? Interview residents (especially seniors) about wait times, health/safety impacts (missing medical appointments, isolation)
DOB data: cross-reference elevator complaints against alteration permits—are buildings deferring elevator modernization despite filings for other work?
Investigate whether DOB inspection capacity (CB budget request #01) is adequate to enforce elevator maintenance; interview CB about complaint trends

themes_detail.label: Sewer System Stress
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints spiked to 11 three weeks ago versus a baseline of 2.9 per week—a 283% increase (z-score: 4.28)—raising concerns about water quality, flooding risk, and potential public health hazard in areas with aging underground infrastructure.
evidence: 11 sewer complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.28, severity: high)
Complements 402 plumbing complaints and 197 water leak complaints (90-day total), indicating systemic water/waste infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: DEP data: is sewer backup activity elevated in CD 202? Are there known aging pipes requiring replacement in Hunts Point/Longwood corridor?
CB budget request for 'other capital budget request for DEP'—verify whether sewage infrastructure upgrade requests have been funded or deferred
Site investigation: evidence of sewage overflow, street flooding, or backup in residential basements; interview affected residents
